newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon medal commemorates "Cana Massacre" victims.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon medal commemorates "Cana Massacre" victims.

text.p: Lebanon issued a medal on Monday commemorating the deaths of 98 people killed and 101 wounded in April when Israeli gunners shelled a U.N. post in south Lebanon where they were sheltering from Israeli bombardments.
The Bank of Lebanon said in a newspaper advertisement the bronze medals, minted in France, were for sale and the proceeds would go to an aid committee.
The victims were civilians crowded into the camp of Fijian peacekeeping troops at the village of Cana.

A U.N. investigation ordered by then secretary-general Boutros Boutros-Ghali found that eight Israeli heavy artillery anti-personnel shells exploded over the camp and five high explosive shells exploded on impact inside it.
A U.N. report said it was unlikely that the shelling of the camp was the result of a mistake by Israeli gunners, but this possibility could not be completely ruled out.

The disaster occurred during a 17-day Israeli land, sea and air blitz against Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon that drove hundreds of thousands of people from their homes in the south, caused up to $500 million damage and killed up to 200 people, mostly civilians.
